title: Continuous telemetry can enable linkage of sessions and contexts to the same wearer
description: The wearable receives a rich, repeated stream of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps from the wearer. Even if direct identifiers are absent in this flow, the combination of persistent sensor patterns, location traces, and timing can act as a quasi-identifier that links multiple observations and contexts to the same person.
assumptions: The device or associated system can persist or correlate telemetry over time rather than treating each reading as isolated.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context did not include a linkage-specific node id.

title: Telemetry reveals sensitive information beyond basic device operation
description: Heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps can disclose identity and highly sensitive inferences such as home/work locations, routines, travel patterns, exercise habits, and potentially health-related conditions. This makes the incoming flow privacy-invasive in itself.
assumptions: The wearable or downstream system can access and interpret the raw telemetry in sufficient detail.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context did not include an identifiability-specific node id.

title: Continuous collection enables detectability of wearer presence and activity
description: Regular telemetry updates, especially GPS and timestamps, make it possible to detect when the wearer is present, moving, sleeping, exercising, or at a particular place/time. The mere existence or pattern of data on this flow can therefore reveal activity states.
assumptions: Telemetry is collected at a frequency sufficient to distinguish activity or presence patterns.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context did not include a detectability-specific node id.

title: Wearer may be unaware of the extent of personal data continuously shared with the device
description: By simply wearing the device, the user may not fully understand that continuous operation captures multiple categories of personal data, including location and time-correlated sensor telemetry, and that this may allow extensive profiling and inference.
assumptions: Not all captured data categories, sampling frequency, or downstream uses are made obvious to the wearer at the moment of collection.

title: Collection of continuous GPS and health-related telemetry may exceed necessity or valid consent expectations
description: This flow captures a broad set of personal data continuously, including precise location and potentially health-related signals. If all categories are not strictly necessary for the stated purpose, or if consent and legal basis do not clearly cover continuous collection and secondary uses, the flow creates non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy requires purpose limitation, data minimization, transparency, and where relevant explicit consent for sensitive data processing.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context did not include a non-compliance-specific node id.

description: The wearable sends exercise sessions, GPS traces, device identifier, and timestamps to the companion app. This may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for core synchronization, especially precise GPS history and persistent device identifiers, violating data-minimization expectations if full fidelity is not required for the app feature being supported.
assumptions: Assumes the companion app does not need the full precision or full history of all synced fields for every sync operation.

title: Linkability of multiple activity batches through stable device identifier
description: Including a stable device id in each sensor batch can allow the companion app to link multiple exercise sessions and GPS traces to the same individual over time, building a long-term activity profile beyond what may be necessary for basic synchronization.
assumptions: Assumes the device id is persistent across syncs and accessible to app-side logic or downstream analytics.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; applicability of linkability to this Process->Process flow is well supported by the mapping context.

title: Identifiability of the user from GPS traces and timestamps
description: The synced GPS traces combined with timestamps and exercise-session data can directly or indirectly identify the user, for example by revealing home/work locations or unique movement patterns, even if no explicit name is included in the flow.
assumptions: Assumes the app can access raw or near-raw location history and timestamps.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; the context supports identifiability as applicable to Process->Process flows.

title: Detectability of user activity from synchronization events and metadata
description: The existence, timing, frequency, and size of synchronization batches may reveal that the user performed workouts or was active at particular times, even aside from the content itself. Observing the flow or its metadata can therefore disclose the occurrence of sensitive behavior.
assumptions: Assumes sync timing correlates with user exercise sessions and that app-side components or observers can access flow metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; detectability is inferred from metadata leakage on this flow.

The flow can therefore create a non-compliance risk with consent, transparency, and purpose-limitation requirements.

title: Excessive health-log collection and storage
description: The mobile app may write more health data to the store than is strictly necessary for the app’s stated purpose, such as overly granular calorie, weight, or exercise histories. This creates avoidable disclosure because intimate lifestyle and health-related personal data are persisted in the datastore beyond what is needed.

title: User may be unable to repudiate submitted health-log entries
description: When the app writes health logs to storage, the system may create a durable record tying the entry to the user account without preserving evidence of user review, correction, or contestability. The user could later be unable to deny or challenge that a particular weight, calorie, or exercise entry was submitted by them.

title: Insufficient transparency about storage of health logs

title: Writing health logs without valid consent or another lawful basis

title: Excessive collection/storage of precise location traces

If the full precision or retention is not strictly necessary for the feature, this flow may disclose more personal data to the system than required, violating data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes the feature could operate with reduced precision, reduced frequency, aggregation, shorter retention, or on-device processing instead of storing full raw traces.

title: Location history store can identify the user through longitudinal traces
description: Persisting GPS traces with timestamps in the location history store makes the data strongly identifying even if direct identifiers are absent. Repeated spatiotemporal points can single out an individual and re-identify them from routine patterns or linkage with external datasets.

title: Stored location history enables profiling and inference of sensitive behavior
description: A location history store containing timestamped GPS traces enables derivation of habits, frequented places, religion, health visits, political activity, and social relationships. This supports detectability/inference of highly sensitive patterns beyond the apparent purpose of recording locations.

title: Users may be unaware of the extent of location-history persistence

Precise location data often requires explicit consent, strict purpose limitation, and limited retention.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdiction or product policy imposes consent, necessity, purpose-limitation, or retention constraints for precise location data.

title: Cross-session location history enables linkability of separate user activities

This creates a linkability threat because otherwise separate activities become correlated into a single longitudinal behavior record.

The analytics result may therefore enable identification or re-identification of a data subject.

description: The flow sends analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset from the Health Analytics Service to an external cloud provider for hosting and replication. Because the transferred dataset includes full health and location data, there is a credible risk that more personal data than strictly necessary is disclosed to a third party, violating data minimisation and increasing privacy impact.

description: Even if direct identifiers are limited, transferring analytics models together with hosted analytics data can disclose sensitive information indirectly. Models, derived features, logs, or metadata may enable inference of health status, location patterns, or membership of individuals in the dataset once replicated to the cloud provider.

description: The flow places the full health and location dataset with a third-party cloud provider for hosting and replication. If users did not consent to third-party hosting, international transfer, or secondary processing required for replication and infrastructure operations, this flow may process highly sensitive data without a valid consent scope or other appropriate legal basis.

title: Cloud provider role may be insufficiently transparent to data subjects
description: Because the data are hosted and replicated at a third-party cloud provider, data subjects may be unaware that their sensitive health and location data are processed by an external infrastructure provider, where replication occurs, and which jurisdictions or sub-processors are involved. uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort; threat applicability depends on actual transparency provided to users.

The replication of the full dataset enlarges the context in which re-identification can occur.
